sector_model: Consumer internet marketplace and platform: gross bookings, take rate, FCF after SBC; investment revaluations excluded from earnings power
thesis: Uber Technologies (NYSE: UBER), global mobility, delivery and freight marketplace. Q3 2026 10-Q (0001543151-26-000041, filed 2026-11-04) and earnings release (8-K 0001543151-26-000039). Q3 gross bookings 59.8B USD (+20%; mobility 29.5B +18%, delivery 28.5B +22%, freight 1.8B +35%); revenue 14,766M (+9.6%; mobility revenue -2%, delivery +23%); income from operations 1,447M (1,113M); adjusted EBITDA 2,963M (+31%, 5.0% of bookings, no longer a key management measure). GAAP net income 512M (EPS 0.25) vs 6,626M a year ago, which held a 4,046M tax benefit and large other income; Q3 2026 other expense of 616M includes a 476M pretax loss on equity investment revaluations, so GAAP is not earnings power either way. TTM (FY2025 10-K plus 9M26 minus 9M25, XBRL): revenue 56,526M, operating cash flow 10,735M, capex 314M, FCF 10,421M (matches company TTM figure), SBC 2,065M so FCF after SBC 8,356M, net income 3,465M. Shares 2,041.9M (10-Q cover, 2026-10-30), market cap about 142.3B at 69.69, so FCF yield 7.3%, 5.9% after SBC, 41x TTM GAAP earnings (distorted by revaluations). Q4 guide: bookings 63.25-65.25B (+18-22% cc), adjusted EBITDA 3.13-3.23B, non-GAAP EPS 0.95-0.99. Balance sheet 2026-09-30: cash 9,558M, short-term investments 510M, non-current investments 7,975M (equity stakes), restricted investments 8,768M (insurance related, not free), long-term debt 15,664M (10,521M at 2025-12-31; current portion unread). Buybacks 4,279M in 9M26 (about 56.6M shares), 902M spent on acquisitions in Q3. Market view: price near 70 versus 52 week range suggests worry over autonomous vehicle disruption and competition; evidence against that is 20% bookings growth with rising margin and 7% FCF yield. What closes the gap: sustained bookings growth near 20% with operating income growth ahead of revenue and buybacks absorbing SBC.
counterthesis: Autonomous vehicle makers could take mobility supply or pricing and Uber is spending (debt up 5.1B in nine months, acquisition purchases) to partner or own. Mobility revenue fell 2% while bookings rose 18%, which points to business model or accounting changes (agency versus principal, driver incentives) that were not read in MD&A. FCF includes working capital and insurance reserve effects, and restricted investments of 8.8B back insurance liabilities. SBC of about 2.1B is a real cost. Q3 GAAP net income fell 92% on revaluation swings and prior tax benefits, so reported EPS is unreliable. Legal and regulatory risk (driver classification, insurance costs, antitrust, tax) in the 10-Q notes was not read. Freight revenue is flat to growing only via acquisitions. Peer multiples (DASH, LYFT, GRAB, BKNG) and Uber's own history were not compared.
invalidation: Thesis fails if gross bookings growth drops below about 12%, FCF falls with operating income, debt keeps rising to fund deals without matching cash flow, autonomous vehicle competitors win key cities, or a legal ruling forces worker reclassification costs.
